properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 28 at 4:08PM MST until August 28 at 7:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Antelope Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 700 PM MST /800 PM MDT/.

* At 408 PM MST /508 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the Antelope Creek basin. Between 0.15
and 0.4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.25 to 0.75 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Antelope Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Antelope Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Coconino County.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower Antelope Canyon, Owl Canyon, Rattlesnake
Canyon and Porcupine Canyon.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Antelope Creek.
properties.instruction:
Get out of Antelope Canyon and other area slot canyons immediately!
Deadly flash flooding is imminent or occurring!

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 7:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 7:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Dust Storm Warning issued August 28 at 4:32PM PDT until August 28 at 5:15PM PDT by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Dust Storm Warning for...
West central Imperial County in southeastern California...

* Until 515 PM PDT.

* At 432 PM PDT, a wall of dust was along a line extending from
Holtville to Imperial to near El Centro Naval Airfield, moving
north at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Less than a quarter mile visibility with strong wind in
excess of 50 mph.

SOURCE...Doppler radar.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

* This includes the following highways...
CA Route 78 between mile markers 14 and 30.
CA Route 111 between mile markers 15 and 31.
CA Route 86 between mile markers 13 and 35.

Locations impacted include...
Brawley, Westmorland, Alamorio, and Wiest.
properties.instruction:
Dust storms lead to dangerous driving conditions with visibility
reduced to near zero. If driving, avoid dust storms if possible. If
caught in one, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep your
foot off the brake.

Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

CMAMtext: NWS: DUST STORM WARNING til 5:15 PM PDT. Be ready for a sudden drop to zero visibility.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: DUST STORM WARNING for this area until 5:15 PM PDT. Be ready for sudden drop to zero visibility. Pull Aside, Stay Alive! When visibility drops, pull far off the road and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights off and keep your foot off the brake. Infants, the elderly and those with respiratory issues urged to take precautions.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 28 at 9:43AM CDT until August 30 at 4:36AM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Illinois...

Wabash River from Hutsonville to Vincennes.

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River from Hutsonville down
to Vincennes. The river has crest. Flooding should come to an end on
the Wabash during the weekend.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Vincennes.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Agricultural lands and some oil fields
flood.  Several township roads about 1.25 miles south of St.
Francesville and River Road between Billett Road and Lincoln
Memorial Bridge in Lawrence County are flooded.  Extensive flooding
of Kimmell Park at Vincennes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM CDT /9:45 AM EDT/ Friday the stage was 18.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 AM CDT /9:45 AM EDT/ Friday was 18.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling to 4.6 feet Monday,
September 07.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 945 PM CDT /1045 PM
EDT/.

* Special Marine Warning for...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...

* Until 745 PM EDT.

extending from Merritt Island Wildlife Refuge to Cocoa to 11 nm
west of West Melbourne, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

miles away from a thunderstorm.
